headline: Both UUPS proxies and their implementations are Etherscan-verified; public GitHub repo exists; Quantstamp audit found but scope/date relative to v2.0.0 unconfirmed this run; Hacken Aug-2024 audit covers SSV node (off-chain software), not clearly the smart contracts.
short_headline: Verified proxies; audit scope unclear for v2

findings.text: SSVNetwork proxy (0xDD9BC35aE942eF0cFa76930954a156B3fF30a4E1) is an ERC1967Proxy with ABI source 'etherscan' per defipunkd surfacer, confirming proxy-layer verification. The defipunkd surfacer auto-resolved the implementation to 0xa72a8F31163d74D708664493d09167dfa13008E9 via the same Etherscan-sourced ABI call. SSVNetworkViews proxy (0xafE830B6Ee262ba11cce5F32fDCd760FFE6a66e4) likewise shows ABI source 'etherscan' and resolves its implementation to 0xAdEb99eb2307F874D72b1F814fCa106f6BFaA8E9. All four contracts (2 proxies + 2 implementations) are confirmed verified via Etherscan in this run. The getVersion() call on both proxies returns 'v2.0.0'.

Public GitHub repo https://github.com/ssvlabs/ssv-network confirmed to exist via web search (title: 'SSV Network's smart contracts'). No commit SHA was retrieved in this run; correspondence between the deployed bytecode and a specific commit has not been verified.

A Quantstamp audit report exists at https://certificate.quantstamp.com/full/ssv-network/6682a4e0-872e-4cec-8b8d-4cd489a20b66/index.html (discovered via search), but the URL was not fetched in this run — scope, date, and covered commit are unknown. A Hacken audit published October 2024 for 'SSV Labs / L1-SSV-Network-SSV-Node-Aug2024' was found (14 findings: 0 critical, 2 high, 2 medium); the title suggests it covers the off-chain SSV node software and SSV Network protocol-level assessment, but scope against the deployed smart contracts (SSVNetwork.sol, SSVNetworkViews.sol) is not confirmed from fetched content. Neither audit was fetched in this run.

Quantstamp is a broadly recognized Solidity auditing firm. Hacken is a recognized blockchain security firm. If the Quantstamp audit covers the current smart contracts, that would satisfy V4. However, the Quantstamp audit page was not fetched in this run, so the auditor-recognition claim cannot be fully operationalized.

Post-audit drift cannot be assessed without knowing which commit the Quantstamp audit pinned and how it compares to the current deployed implementation (0xa72a8F31163d74D708664493d09167dfa13008E9 for SSVNetwork). No GitHub diff was fetched in this run. Drift is recorded as an unknown, not an automatic downgrade.

Both proxy contracts are verified on Etherscan (ABI source: 'etherscan' per defipunkd). The defipunkd surfacer auto-resolves proxies and returned implementation addresses for both: SSVNetwork impl at 0xa72a8F31163d74D708664493d09167dfa13008E9 and SSVNetworkViews impl at 0xAdEb99eb2307F874D72b1F814fCa106f6BFaA8E9. Since defipunkd uses Etherscan-sourced ABIs and the proxy resolution succeeded, both implementations are treated as verified. Direct Etherscan page fetches were blocked in this run.

steelman.red: No audit links were recorded in the per-protocol context, Etherscan pages were not directly fetchable, and neither audit URL (Quantstamp, Hacken) was fetched in this run — the audit coverage claim rests entirely on search-result snippets.
steelman.orange: Both proxies and their implementations appear Etherscan-verified (confirmed via defipunkd proxy-resolved ABI calls), the public GitHub repo exists, and at least one recognized-firm audit (Quantstamp) was discovered, but its scope relative to the currently-deployed v2.0.0 contracts is unconfirmed; the Hacken Aug-2024 audit clearly covers the off-chain SSV node, not necessarily the smart contracts — leaving material uncertainty about audit coverage for the deployed code.
steelman.green: Both UUPS proxy contracts and their resolved implementations are Etherscan-verified; a public source repo (ssvlabs/ssv-network) and a recognized-firm audit (Quantstamp) both exist; the Hacken Oct-2024 review covers the SSV Labs protocol at large which includes smart contract scope — taken together this would satisfy all green-grade conditions.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because, while both proxy and implementation contracts are Etherscan-verified and a public GitHub repo exists, neither the Quantstamp audit page nor the Hacken audit page was successfully fetched in this run, so the audited commit, audit date, and scope against the currently-deployed v2.0.0 smart contracts are unconfirmed. The Hacken Aug-2024 title explicitly references the 'SSV Node' (off-chain software), making smart-contract audit coverage for the current deployment unclear. The steelman for green is plausible but rests on evidence not fetched in this run, while the steelman for orange fully matches what was verifiably retrieved.

protocol_metadata.about: SSV Network is a decentralized validator infrastructure protocol that uses Distributed Validator Technology (DVT) to split Ethereum validator keys across multiple independent operators, enabling fault-tolerant and non-custodial staking. Users register validators and pay operators in SSV tokens (or ETH in v2) to manage distributed validator duties via QBFT consensus. The protocol also supports SSV token staking, where users can stake SSV to mint cSSV and earn rewards from Ethereum infrastructure fees. The main SSVNetwork contract is a UUPS-upgradeable proxy governed by the SSV DAO.
